pairs.subject: embedded-db
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/cache.rs:343 Cache eviction executes destructive deletions directly on the database without dry-run safety rails, usage accounting, or an observable prune ledger.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/cache.rs:307 Cache purge deletes expired entries immediately without a default dry-run mode, usage accounting, or an observable prune ledger.
crates/core/src/cache.rs:113 Cache reads query the pool directly without recording latency into bounded rings or reporting slow operation counts.
crates/core/src/cache.rs:300 Cache writes acquire pooled connections anonymously without measuring acquisition latency, tracking caller labels, or detecting pool contention.
crates/core/src/cache.rs:28 Eviction per-pass limit is chosen as a fixed magic number rather than derived from engine page size, memory budget, or lock duration.
crates/core/src/cache.rs:27 Cache eviction is designed for fixed hourly passes rather than being gated by an activity gauge and yielding between chunks.
crates/core/src/backup.rs:149 Backup retention prunes exclusively by the tool's own prefix marker, safely preserving operator copies and sibling databases.
crates/core/src/backup.rs:239 Pre-migration backup uses SQLite's native VACUUM INTO to produce a consistent single-file snapshot capturing committed WAL state without risking torn sidecars.
crates/core/src/backup.rs:221 Backup failures do not classify corruption or quarantine the handle, continuing migrations despite potential storage failure.
crates/core/src/cache.rs:230 Cache queries are point lookups and bounded log folds that do not justify a separate column-oriented analytics engine.
crates/core/src/cache.rs:39 The HTTP cache operates entirely on standard SQLite features without loading in-process extensions or registering custom collations.
